note: Based on the actual bread-demand dataset (aernoudt_bread_daily_all_years.csv) tested against EDA and Preprocess earlier in this build. Demonstrates both leakage rules: fit_on='train_split_only' for the group-aggregation-style case, and fit_on='row_local_causal' for lag/calendar features.

content.reasoning: dropped num_items_sold, non_bread_quantity, bread_revenue as leakage per EDA; day_of_week encoded as ordinal

context.reason: time_series_analysis and recommended_strategy needed to decide which derived features are worth creating for this forecasting task

time_series_analysis.trend: confirmed real decline — mean daily bread_quantity fell ~28% from 2011 to 2021, not noise
time_series_analysis.seasonality: day-of-week pattern present — Sunday and Saturday notably higher than weekdays
time_series_analysis.stationarity: non-stationary — the confirmed trend means mean demand shifts over the series, not stable
time_series_analysis.autocorrelation: strong at lag 7 (weekly cycle) — today's demand correlates with demand exactly one week prior more than with adjacent days

recommended_strategy.narrative: Given only ~10 candidate features remain after dropping leakage columns, an incremental forward-selection posture isn't necessary — start broader and let embedded importance from a tree-based model prune the weak ones.

1.formula: value at the last OBSERVED period at or before target_date - 1
mean of the last 7 OBSERVED periods at or before target_date - 1

7.formula: median of the last 13 observations on target_date's own weekday, all at or before target_date - 7

input.mode_reasoning: first Feature Engineering call this run — building on Preprocess's latest output

features_created.name: naive_h7_seasonal_median_w13
features_created.trigger: baseline Part B selected this rule as the strongest naive predictor for h=7 on train rows
features_created.formula: median of the last 13 observations on target_date's own weekday, every one at or before target_date - 7 calendar days; walks back to the last OBSERVED period, never a fixed date
features_created.reasoning: hands the h=7 model a decent forecast to correct rather than a level to rebuild from lags; selected per horizon because the rule that wins at h=1 is not the rule that wins at h=7
features_created.max_horizon_reasoning: computed at origin target_date - 7; used at any longer horizon it would read the series after that model's origin, which is a leak

verification.method: rescore the built column on train rows and compare to the baseline's own number for the same rule

features_created.lag_nan_fill: first 13 weeks of the series have no full window; NaN retained and declared native, LightGBM handles it

relevance_check.note: high by construction -- recorded, never used as a drop or leakage signal for a protected column

features_created.name: bread_quantity_lag_7
features_created.formula: bread_quantity shifted 7 rows (1 week) back, per row's own history only
features_created.reasoning: EDA found today's demand correlates more with demand exactly one week ago than with adjacent days — a direct lag feature operationalizes this rather than leaving the model to rediscover a pattern already confirmed statistically
features_created.min_horizon_reasoning: computable at an origin one period before the target; a lag-7 value is available for every horizon up to 7, and this field is what Training uses to build each horizon's feature subset

features_created.name: is_weekend
features_created.formula: 1 if day_of_week is Saturday or Sunday, else 0
features_created.reasoning: the weekend effect EDA found is binary in nature (weekend vs. weekday), not a full 7-level day-of-week distinction — this collapses day_of_week into the specific contrast that actually matters, which may be an easier signal for some model families than 7 separate categories

features_created.name: time_index
features_created.trigger: eda.target.time_series_analysis.trend — confirmed real ~28% decline over the series, non-stationary
features_created.formula: sequential integer index of each row's position in chronological order
features_created.reasoning: a non-stationary target with a confirmed trend needs an explicit way for the model to represent 'how far into the declining series is this row' — without this, a model trained on early years would systematically over-predict later years

naive_predictors_built.nan_fill: first row only; dropped from train window
first 7 rows; NaN retained as native
first 13 weeks; NaN retained as native

protected_features_status.blocking_clarification: naive_h1_trailing_mean_w7_redundancy -- correlates 0.91 with naive_h1_last_value; kept pending the user's answer

horizon_feature_subsets._note: features filters on BOTH bounds: min_horizon <= h (computable at the origin) and known_future_horizon >= h (its target-date value is knowable when the forecast is made). evaluated_at says which anchor each feature is read at; dropped_not_known_future lists what this horizon loses because no forecast reaches that far. A feature below its known_future_horizon is DROPPED for that horizon, never silently replaced by its stale origin value.

output.horizon_feature_subsets_note: h=14 and h=30 lose every short lag, which is the mechanical reason their error is higher - stated here rather than rediscovered in residuals

clarification_needed.question: Drop naive_h1_trailing_mean_w7, which correlates 0.91 with naive_h1_last_value, or keep both?
clarification_needed.description: Both are protected h=1 naive predictors. The redundancy screen would normally drop the weaker one, but a protected feature is never dropped on this node's judgment -- the column is kept and the question is put to the user.
clarification_needed.recommendation_reasoning: 0.91 is below the 0.98 deduplication threshold the baseline already applied, so the two carry different information at the margin; the cost of keeping one extra column is one feature slot against a train set of 1,847 rows
clarification_needed.impact_if_wrong: one redundant column in the h=1 model; costs nothing measurable if kept, costs a rebuild of the h=1 feature set if dropped and later wanted back

plots.reason: verify the lag-7 feature's relationship with the target visually matches the strong correlation found in the relevance check

prediction_time_availability_audit._note: One entry per feature. min_horizon is the lower bound (when it becomes computable at the origin); known_future_horizon is the upper bound (how far ahead its target-date value is knowable). Both are required on every non-target feature.

wx_temperature.reasoning: a public forecast exists ~7 days out; beyond that the target-date value is unknowable and the feature is dropped rather than read at the origin, which would be a stale observation of a variable with no memory

comp_any_holiday.reasoning: a published closure calendar; confirm the window rather than assuming it extends indefinitely

dow_Monday.reasoning: null = unbounded; the date is known arbitrarily far ahead

bread_quantity_lag_1.reasoning: a realisation of the target; never knowable past the origin, so it stays an origin-anchored lag

prediction_time_availability_audit._serving_mismatch_warning: Where a known-future feature is trained on OBSERVED target-date values but served on FORECAST ones, every score from it is an upper bound. State it here, and train on archived forecasts where they exist.

target_representation._note: Per model family where families differ. A family that cannot consume a transformed target does not impose raw levels on families that can.

tree.trigger: significant downward trend in EDA target.time_series_analysis.trend
tree.reasoning: a gradient-boosted tree predicts a leaf constant averaged from training targets, so with level targets its output cannot leave the training range; on a declining series that is a floor no feature can lift

classical_arima.reasoning: ARIMA-family fits model the level directly and cannot consume a ratio target

override._note: Set only when a disqualifying trigger is overridden. Name the family that required it. The override is VOID the moment that family stops being a live candidate, and the decision returns to the representation table. Diagnosis reads this: a champion from a family that never needed the override, while the override is still in force, is a finding and a routing trigger back to feature_engineering.

example_if_set.expires_when: classical_arima is no longer a live candidate

horizon_construction._note: Targets are joined on row_date + h in the series' calendar unit, never by positional shift. These are the realised gaps, recorded so the check is auditable: if median_gap_days != h the column is not what its name says. Split by regime where one exists - a construction that holds on one side and not the other is exactly what this catches.

counter_example.why_rejected: 30 rows on a Monday-filtered frame is five six-day weeks, so the model learns 'same weekday as origin' and is +2 weekdays wrong once the shop trades 7/7
